title: Advanced RAG architectures
summary: A fixed pipeline (retrieve once, answer once) handles most document questions. Some questions need more: one that spans documents and structured data, small talk that needs no search, chunks that turn out irrelevant, an answer that drifts from its sources, facts connected across documents, a chart. This module builds each architecture that handles one of those: **agentic RAG** with a tool per source, **corrective RAG** and **Self-RAG** as LangGraph graphs, **GraphRAG** over extracted triples, and **multimodal RAG**. Production gets a knowledge agent, measured against the Module 7 answerer.
learn: **Agentic RAG**: retrieval as a tool; one tool per knowledge source; the agent decides whether, where and how often
**Corrective RAG**: grade the chunks, rewrite and retry, or say so, as a LangGraph
**Self-RAG**: grade the answer for support and relevance, regenerate, give up
**GraphRAG**: triples into a graph, multi-hop answers by walking it
**Multimodal RAG**: images described, indexed beside text, answered with the original image
flow:
question → knowledge agent ─┬─ search_documents (production Retriever) → numbered sources
                             ├─ query_menu_and_orders (read-only SQL) → rows
                             └─ no tool (small talk)
           ← loops until it can answer, citing [source files]

labs.explain:
Retrieval as a **tool**: the agent decides whether to search (not for 'hi'), how often, and with what query. Then production's knowledge agent with **one tool per source**: document search and read-only SQL over the menu and orders, on aggregate and multi-hop questions.

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

notes.text: content_and_artifact: the model reads sources, the app keeps the Documents.
After loading, the connection can't write anything.

labs.explain:
**Corrective RAG** as a LangGraph: retrieve, **grade** every chunk with an LLM, and if none is relevant **rewrite** the query and retry once, then **give up** honestly. The table shows the path each question took.

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

notes.text: The edge chooses generate, rewrite or give up.

labs.explain:
**Self-RAG** checks the answer: a **hallucination grader** (is every claim supported?) and an **answer grader** (does it address the question?), in a loop that regenerates until both pass, run on a deliberately fabricated answer.

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

**GraphRAG**: an LLM extracts (subject, relation, object) **triples**, networkx stores them as a graph, and a question is answered by **walking two hops** from its entities. Compared with the production retriever on a question that needs facts from two documents.

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

notes.text: Everything within two hops of the question's entities.

labs.explain:
A text embedding model can't read an image, so a **vision model describes** each one; the description is indexed beside the text chunks with the image path in metadata, and the answer gets the **original image** as well as the text.

After a run, **What it covers** shows each learning point with the few lines of code that do it and what they produced.

code.why: Text sources + the original images in one message.

path.title: Production path: the Nimbus knowledge agent
path.summary: Nimbus's documents aren't its only knowledge: the café menu and the orders are tables, and questions about them need counting, not search. The knowledge agent has a tool per source (production's Retriever and read-only SQL), decides which to call, chains them for multi-hop questions and skips them for small talk. Measured against the answerer on 15 questions of five kinds.

steps.title: Tools
steps.explain: `search_documents` wraps the production Retriever (translation, hybrid search, reranking, valid today) and returns numbered sources; the Documents travel as the tool's artifact. `query_menu_and_orders` runs one SELECT over an in-memory SQLite copy of the menu and orders, with the schema and sample values in its description, a row limit, and SQL errors returned as messages the model can fix.
production: For real order data, give the agent a database role with SELECT on specific views, not a file copy (the Data track builds that).
Log every SQL statement an agent runs, with the question that produced it.

steps.title: Agent
steps.explain: `create_agent` with the two tools and a system prompt that says when to use each, to answer only from what they return, and to cite source files. `KnowledgeAgent` owns the SQLite connection and closes it (a context manager), which the lab's first run showed was needed.

notes.text: The connection closes with the agent.

notes.match: - For counting, averaging, totals or comparisons over the café menu or customer orders, use query_menu_and_orders.

production: Cap steps (ModelCallLimitMiddleware, LangChain track Module 5) so a confused agent can't loop.
Every tool call resends the conversation: watch tokens per question.

steps.title: Evaluate
steps.explain:
Same retriever, same model. Measured:

| | documents | aggregates | multi-hop | small talk | unanswerable | tokens / question | p50 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| answerer (Module 7) | 6/6 | 2/4 | 1/1 | 0/2 | 2/2 | 566 | 3.2 s |
| **knowledge agent** | 5/6 | **4/4** | 1/1 | **2/2** | 2/2 | 3,649 | 2.6 s |

The agent handles what the pipeline can't (aggregates via SQL, no search for small talk) at about 6× the tokens per question, and missed one document question the answerer got. Production keeps both: the agent as the entry point, the answerer's verified citations for document answers.
production: Grow the set with real questions per kind: the split between kinds decides whether the agent's extra tokens pay off.
CRAG, Self-RAG and GraphRAG stay in the labs: they cost calls per chunk or per document, and the evaluations didn't show a failure here that they fix.
